# TSMP Core 0.3.0-beta.3

This beta improves decoder throughput and reduces encoder/readback CPU work, temporary allocations and snapshot memory. The wire format, codec IDs, header CRC and finite RPC retry policy are unchanged.

## Changes

- **Faster readback:** reuse the previous validated layout to decode the current header and payload in one GPU readback. Every new header is validated; changed layout or payload length falls back on the same captured image. Equal payload length never means ignoring new contents.
- **Two ordered slots:** overlap up to two independently captured frames and apply completed results in capture order. Disabling the decoder cancels pending results; full slots skip new captures rather than creating an unbounded queue.
- **Combined codec output:** compatible shaders write header and payload bytes directly to the readback target, removing a payload intermediate and a packing draw. Existing third-party shaders retain their fallback.
- **Less CPU work:** use guarded same-type bulk copies and read GPU data into reusable, independently owned byte buffers.
- **Less allocation:** reuse native encoder raster arrays through the optional buffered codec API. Existing custom writers continue to work.
- **Smaller snapshots:** automatically preserve recognized 8-bit or half-float input storage and color interpretation. Unknown/high-precision inputs retain Float32; Udon non-RenderTexture sources retain the conservative fallback.
- **GPU Luma4 encoding:** upload frame bytes and rasterize symbols on the GPU before block expansion. Materials are prepared automatically, owned resources are released on disable/destruction, and the CPU fallback remains available.
- Update English, Korean and Japanese documentation for decoder behavior and codec integration. No extra setup menu is required.

## Measured Improvements

Unity 2022.3.22f1, Windows 11, i9-13900K, RTX 4090, Direct3D11. Luma4, block size 8, sample size 1, one always-sent byte-array field. Udon measurements use Worlds 3.10.4-beta.2, a full client-target UdonSharp compile and the actual SDK Editor VM with GPU readback. Native measurements use a Windows x64 Development Mono Player with stripping disabled.

The baseline is the recorded pre-resource-optimization profile (Core b80194c), which already included the new predicted/two-slot decoder. These are **not** a direct beta.2-versus-beta.3 benchmark. Each profile warms for three seconds and measures twelve seconds.

| Measurement | Before | After | Reduction |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Udon encoder, 720p / 4 KiB / 60 Hz, mean | 11.27 ms | 0.457 ms | 95.9% |
| Udon readback callback, same workload, mean | 3.52 ms | 0.421 ms | 88.0% |
| Udon encoder + decoder submission + callback means | 15.17 ms | 1.248 ms | 91.8% |
| Native publish, 720p / 4 KiB, mean | 3.33 ms | 0.095 ms | 97.1% |
| Native publish, 4K / 32 B, mean | 20.72 ms | 0.141 ms | 99.3% |
| Native 720p, whole-Player median frame GC allocation | 3,686,964 B | 612 B | 99.98% |
| Two 8-bit snapshots, 720p, texel storage | 28.13 MiB | 7.03 MiB | 75% |
| Two 8-bit snapshots, 4K, texel storage | 253.13 MiB | 63.28 MiB | 75% |

The Udon encoder p95 was 0.546 ms and callback p95 was 0.495 ms. The summed means are not a measured frame-time percentile and exclude avatar capture, IK, interpolation, streaming and world rendering. Allocation results cover the entire test Player; collections and a startup spike still occurred. Snapshot savings are not total process/VRAM savings.

**Small payloads also benefited:** the Udon raster helper's CPU time fell from 0.158 to 0.066 ms at 360p / 32 B, and from 0.200 to 0.064 ms at 4K / 32 B.

**GPU tradeoff:** Luma4 adds a conversion draw to remove CPU raster work. Editor GPU timestamp medians for conversion plus expansion were about 16.5 us versus 8.3 us at 720p, and 93.8 us versus 81.0 us at 4K. These exclude upload transfer, readback and world rendering. This is a CPU optimization with a small measured additional GPU draw cost on the tested hardware, not a claim of universally lower GPU time.

## Delivery and Correctness

- Final native and Udon profiles received **361/361 published frames at 30 Hz** and **721/721 at 60 Hz** in the tested small/large cases. The 4K small-payload Udon case sustained about 30 Hz, versus 23.53 Hz in the earlier profile.
- A separate automatic-scheduling test at a 30-FPS Unity cap received **1799/1799 frames over 60 seconds** in both native and Udon two-slot runs. Its native one-slot control received 1579/1800; Udon received 1758/1800. Two slots increased median application latency from about 33.3 to 66.6 ms.
- These finite local tests do not establish lossless video/network transport. A 30-FPS decoder cannot capture every image of an independently changing 60-FPS input.
- Passed full UdonSharp compilation and compiled SDK VM regression, native Windows Player build/execution, 216 changing-source decoder cases, and exact native Gamma/Linear and Udon GPU/CPU Luma4 pixel comparisons.
- Regression covers codec changes, payload growth/shrink, current-header CRC rejection, source overwrite, independent concurrent decoders, ordered completion, disable/re-enable, fallback and repeated RPC deduplication.

## Update

Install **Core 0.3.0-beta.3** together with the matching codec beta(s):

| Package | Version |
| --- | --- |
| Luma4 | 0.0.4-beta.2 |
| RGB16 | 0.0.3-beta.4 |
| RGB20 | 0.0.3-beta.5 |
| Color256 | 0.0.3-beta.4 |

Enable prerelease versions in VCC at https://vpm.kiba.red/ and select these versions explicitly. Ordinary Unity continues to use UPM without VRCSDK. Codec releases require Core 0.3.0-beta.3; update Core first. Existing assets and protocol bytes are preserved. Custom codecs need not adopt the optional APIs.

The authoritative encoded image is `TSMPEncoder.output`. The hidden `outputTexture` is CPU staging and is not refreshed by the GPU path. Advanced opt-outs remain available for prediction, overlap, combined output and GPU Luma4 encoding.

## Scope and Evidence

No live VRChat client, Quest/mobile GPU, other graphics API, OBS/MediaMTX transport, IL2CPP/stripping, populated avatar scene or long-duration soak was verified. Existing decoder shader warnings remain. Full legacy Linear loopback behavior is not newly certified by the separate passing Linear pixel/decoder suites.
